scope: Platform, cloud, network, packaging, and release-boundary review only. No infrastructure, deployment, signing, updater, production service, or application behavior is implemented or approved.

dependencyEvidence.sharedBusinessRuleBoundary: The shared download domain and transfer service own download states, retry, resume, cancellation, destination, and recovery policies. Platform, network, browser, packaging, and update adapters may report capabilities and facts but must not redefine those rules.

deploymentModel.baseline: Local-first desktop application with no required hosted control plane or cloud runtime.
deploymentModel.production: Not declared. Any production environment or deployment requires a separate attributed human approval.

cloudServices.rationale: The candidate core journey can operate locally; adding hosted services would create availability, privacy, identity, cost, compliance, and operational obligations unsupported by approved scope or evidence.

deploymentModel.dataBoundary: Downloaded bytes, partial files, history, URLs, and credentials remain local by default. No production-derived data or credentials may be introduced into test or staging.

networkContract.outboundOnlyBaseline: The transfer engine initiates user-requested outbound HTTP or HTTPS connections. The desktop application exposes no network listener in the baseline.
protocolPolicy: HTTPS is preferred; any HTTP allowance and warning behavior require product and security approval.
Supported URL schemes must be allow-listed; local-file, executable, and custom schemes are rejected unless separately approved.
Redirect count, response-header size, connection attempts, concurrency, and retry delays must be bounded.
Proxy discovery, authentication, certificate-store behavior, IPv4/IPv6, and captive-portal handling must use an approved platform adapter contract.
TLS verification is never disabled by fallback; certificate errors fail visibly through the shared error taxonomy.
Resume is permitted only after validating status, Content-Range, byte bounds, and remote identity; otherwise the domain receives an unsupported-or-changed fact and decides the user-visible path.
Network logs and diagnostics redact URL user-info, sensitive query values, authorization data, cookies, and response secrets.

resourceGuardrails.status: Values require representative measurements and an approved first platform; implementations must fail closed rather than use unbounded defaults.
resourceGuardrails.backpressure: The transfer adapter reports pressure and progress to the shared service; UI refresh frequency is decoupled from network chunk frequency.

adversarialScenarios: Redirect loop or redirect to a disallowed scheme
TLS validation failure or proxy interception
Timeout, DNS failure, connection reset, and offline transition
Server ignores Range, returns malformed Content-Range, changes ETag or Last-Modified, or changes content length
Unknown content length, compressed response, unexpectedly large headers, and insufficient destination space
Application termination during transfer or finalization

platformDeliveryMatrix.status: blocked pending first-platform and architecture approval

packagingCandidates: Disk image or approved store channel

platformDeliveryMatrix.supportedVersions: undecided distributions, desktop environments, and filesystems

browserIntegrationBoundary.baseline: No browser extension, native-messaging host, loopback listener, or browser credential transfer is included.
entryCriteria: Approved MVP inclusion and browser matrix
browserIntegrationBoundary.constraint: If approved later, the adapter submits validated intake commands to the shared domain service and receives safe results; it never gains unrestricted filesystem, process, credential, or state-transition authority.

buildReleasePlan.status: proposed; public release blocked by ADR-04
principles: Build each platform on a pinned, isolated runner for that platform; do not cross-sign on unrelated hosts.
Use locked dependencies, reproducible build inputs where supported, checksums, provenance, SBOM, license review, dependency scanning, and secret scanning.
Keep signing identities outside repository and ordinary test jobs; use least-privilege, audited release-only access with documented rotation and revocation.
Promote one immutable artifact from test to staging evidence; do not rebuild between verification and signing.
Publish neither source release claims nor binaries until license, dependency policy, governance, vulnerability reporting, artifact ownership, signing, and rollback are approved.
stagingGates: Package install, upgrade, rollback, and uninstall tests
buildReleasePlan.updateStrategy: Automatic updates remain blocked. Evaluate platform channels, manual signed releases, and a project-hosted signed updater only after release governance and rollback ownership exist.

observabilityAndOperations.localDiagnostics: Structured local events use safe identifiers and error codes; raw URLs, credentials, headers, cookies, destination paths, and file contents are excluded or redacted.
observabilityAndOperations.telemetry: Absent by default. Any remote telemetry requires a separate approved privacy specification, explicit consent, minimization, retention, deletion, and offline behavior.

costAndCapacity.baselineCost: No always-on cloud runtime cost is justified for the local-first baseline.
expectedCosts: Compatibility hardware or hosted test devices
costAndCapacity.limitation: Numerical budgets require approved platforms, distribution channels, and measured workloads.

networkIntegration: Local deterministic servers exercising redirects, ranges, malformed responses, identity changes, timeouts, throttling, and connection loss
System proxy and trust-store tests on each approved platform
platformRuntime: Clean install, upgrade, rollback, uninstall, restart recovery, insufficient space, locked destination, and file reveal
Offline operation without any cloud dependency
evidenceBeforeImplementationClaim: Dated human platform and MVP decision

traceability.limitation: Governance, licensing, owners, and signing decisions remain unapproved.
The domain behavior and executable application do not yet exist.
Independent disposition is reserved for ENG-15.

implementationNotes: No application code, cloud resources, network services, CI workflow, package, signing material, updater, credentials, database, or deployment was created or changed.
This review preserves the architecture's local-first posture and central shared domain/service boundary.
There is no user-visible behavior in this workstream, so DOM, browser, or desktop runtime verification is not applicable.
Only local, test, and staging are in scope; production requires separate attributed human approval.
knownRisks: The first platform, supported versions, UI foundation, MVP boundary, and meaning of native remain unapproved.
Network resource budgets and proxy, TLS, redirect, and range behaviors are unspecified and unmeasured.
Incorrect range or remote-identity handling can silently corrupt partial files unless adversarial integration tests enforce the shared contract.
Signing keys, package channels, update and rollback ownership, dependency policy, governance, and vulnerability reporting are unresolved.
Linux distribution variance and Windows/macOS security reputation requirements can materially expand maintenance cost.
No executable application or package exists, so platform, accessibility, resilience, performance, and release claims cannot yet be made.
Independent verification remains outstanding and may only be issued by ENG-15.
